summary.text:
Setting the Table for Transition Act

This bill expands eligibility and benefits for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) for some households that contain recently separated veterans.

Under current law, SNAP eligibility and benefits are calculated on a household basis (not individual), and households that meet gross income, net income, and asset limits may qualify for benefits (with exceptions).  Further, a household's net income is used to calculate the monthly benefit amount. 

Under the bill, for a household that includes a member who is a recently separated veteran, only the veteran's personal income is considered when determining income for SNAP eligibility and the monthly benefit amount. Specifically, this applies during the 100-day period that begins upon the date a veteran receives documentation of separation from the military.

dublinCore.dc:description: This file contains bill summaries and statuses for federal legislation. A bill summary describes the most significant provisions of a piece of legislation and details the effects the legislative text may have on current law and federal programs. Bill summaries are authored by the Congressional Research Service (CRS) of the Library of Congress. As stated in Public Law 91-510 (2 USC 166 (d)(6)), one of the duties of CRS is "to prepare summaries and digests of bills and resolutions of a public general nature introduced in the Senate or House of Representatives". For more information, refer to the User Guide that accompanies this file.
